extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent stakeholders (patent practitioners, applicants, and attorneys)
extracted.subtask_short: SME analysis for AI patent claims
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating patent subject matter eligibility (SME) of claims, especially those involving artificial intelligence, consistent with existing MPEP SME guidance and illustrated by new examples. Intended to be applied by USPTO personnel during examination, appeal, and post‑grant proceedings and relied upon by stakeholders when preparing and prosecuting AI‑related patent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of the 2024 AI SME Update
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2024 AI SME Update will assist USPTO personnel and stakeholders in evaluating the subject matter eligibility (SME) of claims in patent applications and patents involving inventions related to Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology (AI inventions). The 2024 AI SME Update does not reflect any new USPTO practice or procedure and is meant to be consistent with existing USPTO guidance, as set forth in the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP), and supplements this guidance to provide further clarity on evaluating SME for AI inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective July 17, 2024. The Update supplements (but does not change) existing MPEP SME guidance (sections 2103–2106.07(c)); it will be incorporated into the MPEP in due course. Office personnel are to follow this 2024 AI SME Update to the extent earlier guidance is inconsistent with it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use existing USPTO SME guidance (MPEP 2103–2106.07(c)) to analyze claims across all technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO’s SME guidance, as found in the MPEP (sections 2103–2106.07(c)), is used to analyze claims across all technologies including AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2024 AI SME Update summarizes that guidance and provides additional discussion of areas particularly relevant to AI inventions, including discussions of Federal Circuit decisions on SME. Examiners and stakeholders should apply that MPEP guidance when conducting SME analyses for AI‑related claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether a claim recites an abstract idea
rubrics_metrics.description: One inquiry addressed by the new examples is whether a claim recites an abstract idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples 47–49 provide exemplary SME analyses under 35 U.S.C. § 101 of hypothetical claims to illustrate how to assess whether a claim recites an abstract idea. Use these examples as fact‑specific illustrations when evaluating similar claim issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine whether a claim integrates an abstract idea into a practical application
rubrics_metrics.description: Another inquiry addressed by the new examples is whether a claim integrates the abstract idea into a practical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples 47–49 illustrate how to analyze whether claimed subject matter that involves an abstract idea is nonetheless integrated into a practical application under the USPTO’s SME framework. Apply the reasoning in the examples to factual situations involving AI inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply SME guidance during examination, appeal, and post‑grant proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Update and its examples are intended to assist USPTO personnel in applying SME guidance during patent examination, appeal, and post‑grant proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the examples as aids for consistent application of the USPTO’s SME framework across procedural contexts (examination, appeal, post‑grant). The examples are fact‑specific and exemplary, not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of the 2024 AI SME Update over inconsistent prior guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent that earlier guidance from the Office, including certain sections of the MPEP (R‑07.2022), is inconsistent with the 2024 AI SME Update, Office personnel are to follow the 2024 AI SME Update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This memorandum expressly directs personnel to apply the Update where inconsistencies exist; the Update will later be incorporated into the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Update does not create new USPTO practice or procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2024 AI SME Update 'does not reflect any new USPTO practice or procedure' and is intended to be consistent with existing guidance while providing further clarity for AI‑related SME questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should not treat the Update as changing substantive practice but as clarifying application of existing MPEP SME guidance to AI inventions; nevertheless, examiners are directed to follow the Update where it supersedes prior inconsistent guidance.
